bug_semantics: Attacker-controlled chart option values can reach HTML or SVG DOM construction. In affected releases, missing or incomplete sanitization permits encoded, control-character, event-handler, dangerous-URI, mutation, or polyglot payloads to survive option binding and execute JavaScript when a user renders or interacts with the chart.
flaw_origin: The earliest surviving public Git object that writes the vulnerable option-to-HTML path is 8413325db50b8ab81606702765a85e38f289b28b ('the birth', 2017-06-08): src/internals/tooltip.js directly passes config.tooltip_contents output to $$.tooltip.html(). Its immediate parent 23369a19d5f457afee675e684512c59c7b5c2036 has no src/internals/tooltip.js, so the vulnerable path is absent there. Later commits added sibling option sinks (including legend templates and custom point SVG), while c69320a25b6a2539809bcd74a3cc13deed80d8a3 applied an incomplete blacklist sanitizer. No finer public member for the initial imported implementation is present in this clone.
ai_marker: No AI marker, AI-authorship trailer, bot identity, or AI attribution appears on the BIC. The commit is authored and committed by Jae Sung Park on 2017-06-08, before modern generative coding assistants.
evidence: The GitHub advisory and CVE record describe CWE-79 in billboard.js before 3.18.0 caused by improper sanitization during chart option binding; the CVE record is PUBLISHED and the advisory is not withdrawn.

git show of 8413325db50b8ab81606702765a85e38f289b28b shows src/internals/tooltip.js newly added with direct $$.tooltip.html(config.tooltip_contents.call(...)) writes; git cat-file confirms the file is absent from parent 23369a19d5f457afee675e684512c59c7b5c2036.

git blame traces the tooltip HTML sink to 8413325db50b8ab81606702765a85e38f289b28b, the legend template sink to 26de1472e, and the custom point SVG DOM insertion to 143282b740ed799af2433b0c94c9212e015977fe, establishing a common unsafe option-binding mechanism with the tooltip path as its earliest public instance.

Commit c69320a25b6a2539809bcd74a3cc13deed80d8a3 (2026-01-13) wrapped several sinks and tplProcess with a blacklist sanitizer but still left entity/control-character and mutation/polyglot bypasses addressed by the direct fix.

Commit 49e079cdd466fc8ba7ab208988181e5b7a5f336b strengthens entity decoding, control-character stripping, event-handler and dangerous-URI filtering, bounds repeated sanitization, validates point type fallback, and adds regression tests for the cited attack families; its message references #4078.

PR #4085 has one member commit, 587dc7a2c41c1e5240da83cc498f2745a8bbaa37, whose tree bf7a5f11ec569c061365208fff37a49f2bf5ff99 exactly matches direct fix 49e079cdd466fc8ba7ab208988181e5b7a5f336b, closing the fix's squash/member history.

Tag 3.17.4 is an ancestor of the fix and does not contain it; tag 3.18.0 resolves to release commit 3abbe9a4e10c02ece62a3cb8e3cf362beceb6099, contains 49e079cdd466fc8ba7ab208988181e5b7a5f336b, and its release notes name #4085/#4078. This matches the advisory boundary '< 3.18.0' / first patched 3.18.0.

The full BIC commit object contains only the human author/committer identity and message 'the birth'; it has no AI marker or AI co-author trailer, and its 2017 timestamp independently excludes the modern generative-assistant provenance at issue.
reasoning: The vulnerability is real and has a vendor-published CVE plus a direct remediation and release boundary. The atomic public origin is the first surviving commit that creates the unsafe option-output-to-HTML flow; its parent lacks that source file. Later sibling sinks and incomplete sanitization changes extend the same mechanism but do not predate the tooltip path. The BIC itself is human-authored in 2017 with no AI evidence, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI. The 2026 remediation commit and its PR member are fixes, not candidates for AI-origin attribution.
